svg.title: freq's heap of the seven best words so far, the worst of them on top: one word replaces the top and sifts down

g.title: Seven words are in the heap, the worst of them, "arthur" (21), on top. The next word, "a" (2643), ranks above it: it belongs among the best seven, and the top must go.
g.text: the same heap as an array: the children of i are at 2i+1 and 2i+2

g.title: Pop: the top, "arthur" (21), comes out, and the last item, "i" (3038), moves into the root. The rule that no item ranks above its children is broken at the root.
g.text: the same heap as an array: the children of i are at 2i+1 and 2i+2

g.title: Sift down: "i" (3038) is compared with the lower ranked of its two children, "sherlock" (97), which ranks below it, so the two swap: "i" (3038) moves from 0 to 1.
g.text: the same heap as an array: the children of i are at 2i+1 and 2i+2

g.title: Sift down: "i" (3038) is compared with the lower ranked of its two children, "holmes" (462), which ranks below it, so the two swap: "i" (3038) moves from 1 to 4.
g.text: the same heap as an array: the children of i are at 2i+1 and 2i+2

g.title: "i" (3038) has reached 4, which has no children (2 * 4 + 1 is past the end): the rule holds everywhere again.
g.text: the same heap as an array: the children of i are at 2i+1 and 2i+2

g.title: Push: "a" (2643) goes in at the end, at 6, as a child of "by" (349).
g.text: the same heap as an array: the children of i are at 2i+1 and 2i+2

g.title: Sift up: "a" (2643) is compared with its parent, "by" (349), and ranks above it, so it stays. The heap holds the seven best words so far, the worst of them, "sherlock" (97), on top.
g.text: the same heap as an array: the children of i are at 2i+1 and 2i+2
